about: Hand-written, number-free inputs to scripts/at-a-glance.ts: which result sets belong to which platform, plain-language descriptions, and the rows of the grid. Every number on the page is computed from the run folders. Review the descriptions and the 'next' lists after each merge.

milestones.label: Final measurement on the final suite (conformance/final-runs, off conformance/full-coverage-final2): every platform row re-run on one suite revision, the current measurement for all of them (the live VTI service and the witness server over DIDComm were not re-run and stay as recorded earlier)

Final measurement on the integrated suite (conformance/integrated): the reference adapter and the platforms measured the same way; superseded by the final measurement above. The witness server and the live VTI service were not re-run and stay as recorded earlier
Re-run after the harness fixes: the same platforms on the suite before the vector review (comparison only, superseded)
The same platforms on the suite before the harness fixes (comparison only, not current)
Re-run after the agreed changes (conformance/agreed-impl); current for the witness server only

supersededBy.about: Run folders whose implementation has more than one current surface: the surface that supersedes them. An empty list marks a record of a later purpose (wallet emit re-runs, promotion gating sets) that supersedes nothing and is listed under supporting records.

rows.label: Core framework
rows.plain: The basic rules every Trust Task document must follow: envelope, proofs, errors, timing, duplicates, the HTTPS door and discovery.

rows.label: Credential tasks
rows.plain: Issuing, requesting, offering and presenting credentials, and asking a person for consent.

rows.label: Ceremony
rows.plain: Relationship ceremonies: proposing and issuing a relationship credential, two-phase commit, ceremony documents and receipts.

rows.label: Single tasks
rows.plain: One check per task type and version, for the access, policy, vault, device and authentication tasks.

rows.label: What the platform sends
rows.plain: Checks of the documents a platform itself produces (the sending side), as opposed to how it handles documents it receives.

rows.label: Rooms
rows.plain: The documents a platform sends for the rooms tasks.

rows.label: 2L profiles (proposed, advisory)
rows.plain: The second-layer profiles (notifications, audit, invitations, join requests, directory and others), receiving and sending. The profiles are the suite's own proposal (profile 2L): advisory, outside the gating counts.

rows.label: Witness sharing (candidate, advisory)
rows.plain: Sharing a credential with a witness. No home in the Trust Tasks repository yet; implemented by one or a few platforms (see the recorded results), possibly adoptable later. Advisory, not an endorsement.

rows.label: Witness server
rows.plain: A witness server reached over real DIDComm messages.

subjects.name: keyring-wallet
subjects.whatItIs: A wallet app that holds a person's credentials and relationships and exchanges Trust Tasks over DIDComm.

surfaces.label: Wallet logic behind a stand-in carrier
Wallet agent over real DIDComm (Credo agent, DIDComm v1)
Wallet agent over real DIDComm (Credo agent, DIDComm v2)
Witness server, the witness session tasks (WIT group)

next: Run the core checks over DIDComm v2 for the cases the v2 row cannot yet carry (documents sent with no sender: DUP-101 to DUP-109 end in an adapter error there) and observe the wallet's retained store over its real repository.
Review the recorded differences, including the push-registration finding (no recipient or issue time), with the maintainers.

subjects.name: truststackers (original)
subjects.whatItIs: The original TrustStackers p2p-trust-stack repository, at its upstream main: a peer-to-peer trust stack with agents, communities and credentials.

notReachable.text: The original repository's upstream main (commit d7ebe8f) has no Trust Task boundary and no conformance adapter that the suite can drive, so nothing could be run against it. This says the suite cannot reach it yet; it is not a defect report.

next: Nothing can be measured until the original exposes a Trust Task boundary (and the adapter that drives it).
Re-run against the original as soon as such a boundary exists there.

subjects.name: VTI
subjects.whatItIs: A community trust service plus an agent service for verifiable credentials and relationships (verifiable-trust-infrastructure).

surfaces.label: Community service, in process (the live-service adapter against the service's own test host)
Sending side: documents built by VTI's own client code

witness-server.reason: VTI's witness tasks belong to a different task family and carrier, so the witness-server checks do not apply (read from VTI's source at the tested version, not from a run).

next: Exercise the community service's governance declaration: enrol a step-up approver and a second administrator, then grant defined roles (the declaration is refused today without them).
Build a host that can push (the agent service's push engine needs a messaging session) so the pushed-document checks (credential-exchange offer, request, present) and send-only checks can run.
Let the in-process community service restart, and run the second-layer checks that only it serves against it.
Re-run the live community service on the current set of checks; it was last run on an earlier, smaller set (the container runtime was not usable here).

subjects.name: Reference adapter
subjects.whatItIs: A small implementation inside the suite, built to behave exactly as the checks expect. It is the suite checking itself: it shows the checks are consistent with each other. It says nothing about any real platform.
next: Keep it green as checks are added; it is the first thing to look at when a new check misbehaves.

shim.name: Stand-in carrier
shim.plain: The platform's own code runs, but the message carrier is replaced by an in-memory stand-in. The result says nothing about the real wire.

in-process.name: In process
in-process.plain: The platform's own handlers run inside one test process, reached over a local loopback door. A library-level result, not a deployed service.

didcomm.name: Real DIDComm
didcomm.plain: A running service exchanges real DIDComm messages with the suite. Closest to real use among the ways here.

in-process-vtc.name: Community service in process
in-process-vtc.plain: The community service's own handlers, router and stores run inside one test process on a loopback port, driven by the same adapter that measures the live service. A library-level result, not a deployed service.

emit.name: Sending side
emit.plain: The documents the platform itself builds are captured from its own client code and checked; nothing is sent to a running service.

live.name: Live service
live.plain: A running deployed service reached over HTTPS.

reference.name: Suite's own adapter
reference.plain: The suite's built-in implementation, used to check the suite itself.
